10. Pipelines

Say you own the Monday report the sales team presents. It reads orders by city, which read the cleaned orders, which read the raw orders feed, and a bad row anywhere below ends up on their slides. Real pipelines are layered like that: cleaned tables feed joined tables feed reports. In sverify the layers are transforms composed directly, each called on the one below. Without a .write in between they fuse into one plan, maintained as one incremental view (chapter 9). .write(sink) stores a layer, as a cache in the middle of a job or as its output; the layers above read the stored table as a versioned source, through its change feed. So an intermediate result is computed once and shared, and only changes flow through the layers. This chapter brings chapters 8 and 9 together: the base layer is the contracted doubled(paid(orders)), and its guarantees keep holding in every state of the pipeline, not only the first.

data.text/markdown:
• paid and doubled have no .write between them, so they fuse into one plan; .write(DeltaSink(...)) stores the result as base. cities and located read base's Delta table, not orders.
  • A contracted transform called on a stored node builds on what that node's plan proved, as in a direct composition: cities requires _.doubled.notnull() of base, which doubled guarantees, so it is checked once, when the node is built, and never on the data. A precondition base doesn't guarantee raises CompositionError right there.
  • sv.group(by_city, by_location) refreshes both reports against the same source versions; base is refreshed and written once for the two of them, upstream first. Its first refresh checked paid's preconditions on all of orders (the requires … (checked on data) lines above).
  • located is a left join, so it is recomputed and diffed on each refresh (chapter 9). Its change would still flow to any node reading it. status() says so:
cities: base@v2, customers@v0
located: base@v2, customers@v0; recomputed (not incrementally maintainable (left join, fetch or window))
base: orders@v0; stored in /tmp/tmpzeeuq3p9/base

Changes, layer by layer

We'll feed the pipeline. Each button changes orders and customers and refreshes both reports. The first is valid; the other two each insert an order that breaks a precondition of paid. We refresh with audit=True, so every batch is also compared with recomputation before it is applied (AuditError otherwise).

data.text/markdown:
Why the guarantees survive every batch

Whoever reads base relies on its guarantees on the hundredth batch as much as on the first. paid's preconditions were checked on all of orders once, on the first refresh. After that, only the batch is checked:
  • row conditions (amount >= 0) on the inserted rows;
  • keys (unique(id)) among the inserted rows and against the keys of the rows the batch keeps.
That is enough, by theorem Spec.update in SubstraitLean/Compose.lean: a table's contract survives a batch if the inserted rows satisfy the row conditions and their keys clash with neither each other nor the kept rows. Triple.maintained then says a contracted view's guarantees hold in the new state. So base satisfies doubled ≥ 0 and is non-NULL after every batch, without ever re-checking the whole table, and the Delta table it is written to records those guarantees with every version, for the layers that read it. The layering itself is Rel.chain_sound (DBSP's chain rule): when a view reads another view's stored result, and gets that view's change as its change table (here, through the Delta change feed), its own update plan is still correct. For a recomputed view, ZSet.diff_correct shows new − old is a valid change to pass on. Each refresh brings the layers up to date upstream first and writes every stored node exactly once per state. If the job stops and restarts, building the same nodes again is enough: the first refresh resumes each stored node from its table when the plan and the source versions match, rather than computing it again. You can now stack transforms into layers that pass only their changes along, store the ones others read, and rely on every contract's guarantees in every state while only the batch is checked. Next up, Engines and SQL runs the same checked plans on Polars and DataFusion, and as SQL for Snowflake and Spark.
